constraints.rule: An anticipated or planned number of discretionary exemptions or waived-area ABAWDs is not observed state practice.
A federal discretionary-exemption allocation is not evidence that a state used any exemption.
An expired waiver is predecessor custody, not a current operative waiver.
Failure to find a current response on an official index is a bounded index/source result, not proof that no request, approval, or waiver exists.
A dated state-page snapshot is not a complete governing period without exact start, end, and successor custody.
A published form or screening template does not establish that it was used in a case or used uniformly.
A state rule, manual, letter, or handbook does not establish uniform frontline practice.
Authority to grant an exemption is not observed exemption use.
Waiver authority is not a waiver request, approval, or current operative period.
A landing page or index is not the complete operative authority/version.
A California, South Dakota, or Washington result cannot be promoted into a national-prevalence claim.
HTTP success or captured bytes are not source admission, field classification, row terminalization, or class closure.
